_comment: Single source of truth for DOZ.AI brand application. Generated from brand/guidelines/brand-guidelines.png (Brand Identity Guide v1.0) plus measurements from tools/derive_logo_variants.py. Do not hand-edit once the renderer depends on it — change the guide or re-run the tool instead. Anything the renderer needs that is absent here is a bug in this file, not a licence to invent a value.

brand.name: DOZ.AI
brand.tone: Modern, minimal, technical, premium. Geometric, soft-edged, symmetrical mark suggesting motion, connectivity and AI systems; bold sans wordmark for a stable, serious tone.

rules.verbatim: Keep all applications strictly monochrome. No vibrant accents.
rules.enforcement: Every colour emitted by the renderer must resolve to a value in color.palette or color.chart.series. Any other hex is a validation failure.

color._comment: The guide prints 8 swatches but only 5 unique hex values — the second row repeats three of the first row's colours under different names. Both vocabularies are recorded so either resolves.

charcoal.alias_note: Listed a second time in the guide as 'Deep Gray / SECONDARY DARK'.

slate_gray.alias_note: Listed a second time in the guide as 'Mid Gray / SECONDARY MID'.

light_gray.alias_note: Listed twice in the guide, both times as Light Gray #EDEDED.

tokens._comment: Semantic names the template and CSS use. Every value is a reference into color.palette — never a raw hex.

usage_notes.text_muted: slate_gray (#5B5B5B) is specified for MUTED ANNOTATIONS only. It clears WCAG AA on both white (6.8:1) and #EDEDED (5.8:1), but body copy stays charcoal (#111111) for comfort at 15px.
usage_notes.surface_container: #EDEDED panels also satisfy the guide's requirement for a solid panel behind any logo that would otherwise sit on a busy background.

chart._comment: EXTENSION, NOT FROM THE GUIDE. The palette offers four values usable on white, which cannot separate 5-7 competitor series. Rather than introduce an accent hue (forbidden by strict_monochrome), this ramp interpolates between existing brand greys. #000000, #5B5B5B and #EDEDED are brand values; #2E2E2E, #8A8A8A and #B8B8B8 are derived. Pending user approval.
chart.approval_note: User approved the derived grey ramp on 2026-08-12. It remains an extension to the printed guide, not part of it — if the guide is ever reissued with an official chart palette, that supersedes this.
chart.series_order_note: Ordered for maximum adjacent-pair contrast, not by lightness, so neighbouring series stay distinguishable.
encoding_rules: Direct-label every series at its endpoint. Do not rely on a colour legend — under monochrome a legend forces the reader to match near-identical greys.
Order categorical bars by value, descending, so position carries meaning alongside fill.
Distinguish line series by dash pattern first and grey second.
Highlight DOZ.AI's own series in #000000; competitors take the remaining ramp steps.
Grid lines and axes use #EDEDED; axis labels use #5B5B5B.

accent._comment: EXPLICIT EXCEPTION to rules.strict_monochrome, authorised by the user on 2026-08-12 for infographics only. The printed guide says 'Keep all applications strictly monochrome. No vibrant accents.' This overrides that for charts and nothing else — the accent must never appear in body copy, headings, rules, panels, logos or any non-chart surface.
accent.purpose: Mark DOZ.AI's own series so the reader finds it instantly. One accent, one job — everything else in a chart stays on the grey ramp.
accent.light_note: Deeper orange holds its own against a #FFFFFF ground; clears the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement for graphical objects.
accent.dark_note: Lifted orange for #000000 grounds — the light value reads muddy on black.
restrictions: Never use for text smaller than 18px — these values are tuned for graphical objects (3:1), not body text (4.5:1).
Never use for more than one series in a chart. If two things need emphasis, the chart is doing too much.
Competitor series always stay on the grey ramp. The accent means 'this is us'.

sans.name: Geist
sans.embed_note: fsType 0 (Installable Embedding) verified with fontTools — legal to embed in the PDF.
sans.fallback_note: The guide's Type Recommendations column suggests 'Inter, Satoshi, or similar', but every specimen in the scale system is labelled Geist. Geist is treated as authoritative; Inter and Satoshi are recorded as documented fallbacks.

h3.label: Subhead
h3.provenance: proposed — the guide defines no H3; interpolated between H2 (24px) and body (15px)

small.label: Small
small.provenance: proposed — the guide defines no caption size; set one step below body

mono.label: Technical
mono.provenance: proposed size — the guide specifies the face and its usage but no size

eyebrow.label: Section eyebrow
eyebrow.provenance: derived from the guide's own section headers ('01 / BRAND DIRECTION'), which are uppercase letterspaced mono

mono_usage.verbatim: Reserved exclusively for metadata, labels, variables, and technical/code parameters.
mono_usage.never: Body copy, headings, or any running prose.

typography.proposed_additions_note: h3, small, mono size and eyebrow are not in the guide. They are recorded with an explicit 'provenance' field so a future reader can tell extracted values from inferred ones.

logo._comment: Geometry measured by tools/derive_logo_variants.py; see brand/brand_metrics.json for the raw measurement.

lockup.description: Primary lockup — symbol above wordmark, transparent background.
lockup.use: Cover page and back page. Preferred on white.

symbol.description: Secondary mark — symbol only, transparent background.
symbol.use: Running header on interior pages, and anywhere space is limited.

clear_space.basis: Height of the dot in the .AI wordmark, per the guide's Clear Space Rules.
clear_space.application: Multiply the rendered logo height by this ratio to get the minimum padding on all four sides.

minimum_size.provenance: The guide states clear-space rules but no minimum size. These are proposed floors below which the wordmark stops being legible in print.

prohibitions: Do not stretch or compress the system assets
Do not add shadows, gradients, outlines, or textures
Do not rotate the symbol or alter its geometry
Do not change the wordmark typography family
Do not place on busy backgrounds without a solid panel
Do not recolor the core marks outside approved monochrome
renderer_obligations: Always set width or height alone, never both, so aspect ratio is preserved (prohibition 1).
Never apply CSS filter, box-shadow, or border to a logo element (prohibition 2).
Never apply transform: rotate to a logo element (prohibition 3).
Place a solid #FFFFFF or #EDEDED panel behind any logo adjacent to a screenshot or chart (prohibition 5).
Use the supplied reversed asset on dark grounds rather than a CSS invert filter (prohibitions 2 and 6).

page._comment: Print geometry for the PDF. Not specified in the guide — chosen to suit an A4 report and recorded here so the renderer has a single place to read them from.
